transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is that my eating has just gotten really off lately. Some days I barely manage to get down a cup of coffee and a granola bar before my shift starts. And I've noticed my scrubs are hanging pretty loose on me, even though I haven't been trying to lose weight at all. It's just... I don't really have an appetite anymore.
Have you noticed any significant weight loss recently, or have you been feeling down or hopeless most days?

Yeah, like I mentioned with my scrubs, I've definitely lost some weight. And as for feeling down... yeah, I have. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling. It just feels like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge for work.
Have you noticed that you don’t take as much pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or time with friends and family?

Yeah, I have. I used to go running over in Van Cortlandt Park pretty regularly, and I liked taking photos while I was out there. I also used to play chess with some buddies of mine. But lately... I don't know, I just tell myself there’s no point. I end up just sitting at home, scrolling on my phone or looking over my budget spreadsheet instead. I just don't have the energy or interest for any of the stuff I used to like.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or like you’re not worth much lately? Like you’re a burden or failing at things you should be doing?

Yeah, I do feel like that a lot. I just... I keep thinking I'm a burden to the clinic where I work, and to my family, too. Like I'm just dragging everyone down. And at work, if I make a small mistake, like... if I'm a little slow turning over a room for the next patient, I just beat myself up over it. I blame myself like I've ruined everyone's whole day just because I was a few minutes behind. It just feels like I'm failing at everything.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or have trouble sitting still lately?

Yeah, it's actually been both, depending on the day. Sometimes at work, I just... I can't sit still. I end up pacing around the supply area, just opening and checking the same drawers over and over. But other times, it's the exact opposite. I move so slowly... like, just drawing up labels or answering a patient's question takes me twice as long as it normally should. It's like I'm moving through mud.
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these symptoms lasted for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yeah, it's been a lot longer than two weeks. The... the steady depression and that loss of interest, it settled in a bit later on, but it's been with me for roughly the past year and four months now. And yeah, it's there most of the day, pretty much every day.
Before this past year and four months, have you ever had a period lasting at least a couple of months where you felt down or lost interest in things?
No, I don't think so. Before this recent stretch, I can't really recall a time where I felt this down for months on end. It's really just been this past year and a half or so that's been like this.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation suggests possible depressive disorder (e.g., major depressive disorder) or eating disorder (e.g., anorexia nervosa) given weight loss, reduced appetite, and lack of intentional dieting. Anxiety and other medical causes of weight loss are also being considered.

The patient endorsed symptoms of depressed mood and significant weight loss, which aligns with major depressive disorder presentations. This likely rules out adjustment disorder (F43.2), acute stress reaction (F43.0), and unspecified stress reaction (F43.9), as well as the eating disorder codes (F50.0, F50.1) as the primary diagnosis given the prominence of mood symptoms. No evidence for nutritional deficiencies (E40, E41, E43) was noted.

The patient reported both psychomotor agitation and retardation, which are key features of severe depressive episodes. This helps narrow the candidates to severe major depressive disorder (F32.2) or severe recurrent depressive disorder (F33.2).

The patient's symptoms have persisted for over a year, indicating a more severe and possibly persistent form of depression. The presence of psychomotor agitation and retardation, anhedonia, significant weight loss, and persistent guilt supports the upgrade from moderate (F32.2/F33.2) to severe (F32.3/F33.3) depressive episode coding. No features of bipolar disorder or psychosis were endorsed to shift the diagnosis elsewhere.
